packs.title: Sacramento, CA: ground + bowls (10 m)
packs.summary: Two rivers held back by levees. Natomas and the Pocket sit 15-25 ft below the Sacramento River at flood stage; FEMA maps Natomas A99 (levee still being built to the 1% standard). Adds ground height offline and how deep water can stand at each spot (behind levees, the basin depth).
packs.label: Ground and bowls, 10 m

packs.title: New Orleans, LA: ground + bowls (10 m)
packs.summary: Much of the city is below sea level inside levees and depends on pumps; heavy rain ponds where the pumps can't keep up. Adds ground height offline and how deep water can stand at each spot (behind levees, the basin depth). Caveat: the drainage-canal floodwalls are thinner than the 10 m grid, so the city's rim reads near lake level and the bowl understates how deep a protection failure could get. Compare the ground with lake and river levels instead.
packs.label: Ground and bowls, 10 m

packs.title: Miami & Miami Beach, FL: ground + bowls (10 m)
packs.summary: High-tide flooding on sunny days, porous limestone under the seawalls, and hurricane surge. Adds ground height offline and how deep water can stand at each spot (behind levees, the basin depth). Caveat: seawalls are thinner than the 10 m grid, and sunny-day flooding comes up through storm drains and porous rock, so compare the ground with the tide rather than relying on the bowl.
packs.label: Ground and bowls, 10 m

packs.title: Norfolk, VA: ground + bowls (10 m)
packs.summary: The fastest relative sea-level rise on the US East Coast; tidal flooding closes streets many times a year. Adds ground height offline and how deep water can stand at each spot (behind levees, the basin depth).
packs.label: Ground and bowls, 10 m

packs.title: Charleston, SC: ground + bowls (10 m)
packs.summary: The peninsula's low streets flood at king tides and in ordinary heavy rain when the outfalls are under water. Adds ground height offline and how deep water can stand at each spot (behind levees, the basin depth). Caveat: the Battery seawall and outfall flap gates are thinner than the 10 m grid; compare the ground with the tide.
packs.label: Ground and bowls, 10 m

packs.title: Houston, TX: ground + bowls (10 m)
packs.summary: Flat land, clay soil and bayous that overtop in heavy rain; Harvey put 50 in of rain on the region. Adds ground height offline and how deep water can stand at each spot (behind levees, the basin depth).
packs.label: Ground and bowls, 10 m

packs.title: New York City (harbor shore), NY: ground + bowls (10 m)
packs.summary: Lower Manhattan, Red Hook and the south Brooklyn and Queens shore flooded in Sandy; basement apartments flood in cloudbursts. Adds ground height offline and how deep water can stand at each spot (behind levees, the basin depth).
packs.label: Ground and bowls, 10 m

packs.title: Boston, MA: ground + bowls (10 m)
packs.summary: Much of downtown, the Seaport and East Boston is filled marsh a few feet above today's high tides. Adds ground height offline and how deep water can stand at each spot (behind levees, the basin depth).
packs.label: Ground and bowls, 10 m

groups.name: Sacramento
groups.why: Two rivers held back by levees. Natomas and the Pocket sit 15-25 ft below the Sacramento River at flood stage; FEMA maps Natomas A99 (levee still being built to the 1% standard).

drains.note: County only: no inlets inside the City of Sacramento

reports.where: CategoryName IN ('Drains Plugged Drain Inlet','Drains Drain Inlet Foreign Material','Drains General')

groups.name: New Orleans
groups.why: Much of the city is below sea level inside levees and depends on pumps; heavy rain ponds where the pumps can't keep up.
groups.caveat: Caveat: the drainage-canal floodwalls are thinner than the 10 m grid, so the city's rim reads near lake level and the bowl understates how deep a protection failure could get. Compare the ground with lake and river levels instead.

reports.where: request_reason in('Catch Basin Not Draining','Catch Basin - Clogged','Street Flooding','Catch Basin Clogged','Street Flooding / Drainage') AND latitude between {s} and {n} AND longitude between {w} and {e}

groups.name: Miami & Miami Beach
groups.why: High-tide flooding on sunny days, porous limestone under the seawalls, and hurricane surge.
groups.caveat: Caveat: seawalls are thinner than the 10 m grid, and sunny-day flooding comes up through storm drains and porous rock, so compare the ground with the tide rather than relying on the bowl.

reports.where: Subject IN ('Flooding or Drainage Issue','Storm Flood or Drainage - City of Miami') AND Latitude BETWEEN {s} AND {n} AND Longitude BETWEEN {w} AND {e}

groups.name: Norfolk
groups.why: The fastest relative sea-level rise on the US East Coast; tidal flooding closes streets many times a year.

drains.where: GENERAL_TY IN ('Catch Basin','Drop Inlet','Yard Basin','Gutter Basin')

reports.where: upper(event_type) like '%FLOOD%' AND latitude between {s} and {n} AND longitude between {w} and {e}

groups.name: Charleston
groups.why: The peninsula's low streets flood at king tides and in ordinary heavy rain when the outfalls are under water.
groups.caveat: Caveat: the Battery seawall and outfall flap gates are thinner than the 10 m grid; compare the ground with the tide.

drains.where: INLETTYPE IS NOT NULL AND INLETTYPE <> 'Pipe'

groups.name: Houston
groups.why: Flat land, clay soil and bayous that overtop in heavy rain; Harvey put 50 in of rain on the region.

reports.where: CASE_TYPE IN ('Flooding','Poor Drainage','Inlet Clogged Needs Cleaning ROW')

groups.name: New York City (harbor shore)
groups.why: Lower Manhattan, Red Hook and the south Brooklyn and Queens shore flooded in Sandy; basement apartments flood in cloudbursts.

reports.where: descriptor in('Catch Basin Clogged/Flooding (Use Comments) (SC)','Street Flooding (SJ)','Highway Flooding (SH)','Catch Basin Clogged','Flooding on Street','Flooding on Highway') AND within_box(location,{n},{w},{s},{e})

groups.name: Boston
groups.why: Much of downtown, the Seaport and East Boston is filled marsh a few feet above today's high tides.
